chunks: Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Hamza ibn Ubayd, from Ismail ibn Abbad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: 'And they cannot encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills,' and its ending is 'And He is the Most High, the Great,' and 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds,' and two verses after it.
ai.seo_question: Which verses in the Quran are included in the description of Ayat al-Kursi according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific verses of Surah Al-Baqarah that Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) recited or referenced on the Day of Judgment, linking the divine attribute of limited human knowledge to the famous Ayat al-Kursi (2:255). The Imam identifies the concluding phrase 'And He is the Most High, the Great' as the end of the verse, followed immediately by the opening of the next verse, 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds' (2:256), and one subsequent verse (2:257). This highlights the continuity of divine praise and the transition from God's absolute knowledge to His lordship over the worlds, a key theme in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the efficacy of these verses in intercession and judgment.

en.hubeali: H 14886 – Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Hamza Bin Ubeyd, from Ismail Bin Abbaad, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws said:

“[2:255] and they cannot comprehend anything out of His knowledge except what He pleases” and its ending “and He is the Most High, the Great”, and Praise be to Allahazwj the Lordazwj of the Worlds, and two Verses after it’ (2:256-257).
en.sarwar: 439. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al-Husayn Bin Sayf, from his brother, from his father, from Abu Bakr Bin Muhammad who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.), recite this Verse as: “[2:214] ‘يَقْرَأُ وَ زُلْزِلُوا ثُمَّ زُلْزِلُوا حَتَّى يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ’ and they were shaken violently, (then they were shaken violently) so that the Messenger said”.
